PullRequest.Title: Remove dedicated workspace generation flows
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Part of #344452.

Related changes: microsoft/vscode-embeddings#143 and microsoft/vscode-docs#10549.

## Summary

- Remove `create_new_workspace` / `copilot_createNewWorkspace`, its `#newWorkspace` reference (historically `#new`), the legacy `/new` intent, dedicated project-setup skills and their settings.
- Remove the workspace-generation prompts, previews, create commands, continuation state, initializer and dedicated tests and fixtures.
- Remove the project-template embedding index, its settings and service registrations, and GitHub content-fetch helpers used only by the retired template workflow.
- Remove the Welcome entry/command, pre-authentication workspace placeholder, and workspace-generation-only shutdown-warning bypass. Preserve normal lifecycle warnings.
- Preserve ordinary file/folder operations, shared chat transfer, notebook creation, and unrelated embeddings. Users can open an empty folder and ask an agent to scaffold a project using its standard tools.
- Add a regression guard for retired manifest surfaces and retained standard tools; update ten prompt snapshots, each removing only `create_new_workspace`.

Follows the merged Welcome-entry removal in #344449; this removes the remaining command and dedicated implementation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate the Copilot extension and open a normal or previously generated workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension contribution/service registration runs during activation. Before the PR, the new-workspace contribution constructed an initializer that read persisted workspace-generation state and could inspect the workspace directory; the PR removes that contribution and its service descriptors, so no new work is placed on activation's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the first workspace directory when persisted new-workspace continuation state matched the opened folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one directory read per activation for a matching persisted generated workspace; zero for ordinary workspaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The initializer contribution was constructed at activation and conditionally read the directory; after the diff the contribution no longer exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Could delay or add work during extension activation for the matching continuation case; this boundary is removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and update persisted extension global state for workspace-generation continuation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per activation and up to one update for a matching record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old contribution consulted a bounded list of up to 30 records; the changed activation path performs none of this work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small activation-path storage work in the retired workflow; removed by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One activation per extension host; the retired initializer examined the first workspace folder and up to 30 persisted workspace-generation records.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The initializer launched one asynchronous update from construction and at most one directory read; the changed path schedules none.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The retired initializer read extension global state. The project-template embedding service was registered lazily and its cold remote/local cache load occurred only when the retired workflow requested it; both registration and workflow are removed. Existing combined-embedding caches are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: contribution and service registration deletions directly eliminate the initializer and project-template service from activation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The backing cost of extension global-state access varies by host, but the diff removes rather than adds it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Activation performs strictly less dedicated workspace-generation setup and introduces no replacement boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ask Copilot to scaffold a project or use the retired #new/newWorkspace workflow
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Previously the dedicated intent/tool could render extra prompts, load a template embedding index, recursively enumerate GitHub template contents, and generate project/file content. The PR removes the manifest surfaces, intent/tool registration, prompt code, repository APIs, and template index. Requests now use pre-existing standard agent tools; this diff adds no implementation or boundary to that path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the project-template embedding cache and rank templates for the dedicated workspace intent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cache load per index instance, then in-memory ranking per dedicated request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold requests could fetch/load the cache and warm requests reused it; the PR deletes the index and its service registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Was on the dedicated template-selection path; now absent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively call GitHub repository contents APIs for directories and fetch content for previewed template files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One contents request per traversed directory and one content request per opened/copied file in the retired template workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dedicated template workflow owned these APIs; repository search confirms no remaining callers or replacement project-template index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directory enumeration blocked template preview construction, while file-content fetches blocked individual preview reads; all are removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Make utility-model requests for one project specification and lazy file contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One specification request per generated preview plus one request for each file whose content was opened/generated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Dedicated previews issued these additional model calls; the changed code does not relocate them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The specification blocked file generation and each file request blocked its preview; the PR removes this generator.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Previously costs scaled with template directory count, files previewed, generated files, and conversation history. After effective removal, dedicated-workflow cardinality is zero; any standard-agent tool cardinality depends on the model's existing tool choices and is not introduced by these hunks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The retired GitHub directory traversal was sequential by directory; generated file content was lazy per opened file. No new limiter, queue, or concurrency burst is introduced because those paths are deleted.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold dedicated template requests could load the versioned project-template embedding cache; warm requests reused the in-memory loaded index. Both positive cache state and the workflow consuming it are removed. Existing standard-agent caches and tools are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for elimination of the dedicated boundaries; low evidence for any increased cost on the standard path, so no finding is warranted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A user asking for scaffolding may still cause existing standard agent tools to run model, terminal, or filesystem operations, but their exact sequence is model-driven and no changed hunk adds or amplifies those existing tools.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The PR removes substantial dedicated network/model work and shortens registered tool metadata; fallback to existing standard tools does not itself prove diff-added performance cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Materialize a generated workspace or file from a preview
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The retired Create Workspace command sequentially read preview content, created directories, wrote each file, updated a tracking file, transferred chat, and opened a folder. The command and providers are removed; the diff adds no equivalent write loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read preview content, create parent directories, write each generated file, and update aiGeneratedWorkspaces.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately one preview read, directory creation, and write per generated file, plus bounded name-stat checks and one tracking-file update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dedicated Create Workspace command performed an O(file count) sequential materialization; no surviving handler in the diff performs it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All file operations completed before the old workspace-open prompt; the entire command is removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer the active chat and execute the open-folder command after materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one transfer and one open-folder command per accepted generated workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old command transferred/opened the generated folder; the retired command has no replacement in these changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurred after file creation and before navigation to the generated workspace; removed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Previously filesystem work scaled linearly with the number of generated files and collision checks scaled with existing same-named sibling folders. The dedicated path now has zero operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The retired file loop was deliberately sequential; no changed path replaces it with parallel work or creates a burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Preview content promises were cached on tree nodes and prior file contents were retained per response. All preview managers and their maps are removed; no new cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: command registration, providers, preview managers, and write implementation are all deleted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Standard agent file tools remain available and can write projects, but their existing implementation and cardinality are unaffected by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. O(file count) dedicated filesystem and retained-preview work is removed rather than amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close or quit VS Code while a supported chat or local agent-host session is active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Shutdown computes the effective reason, checks active sessions, may query native window count for CLOSE, and may show a confirmation. The PR removes a context-key bypass that was set only by the simultaneously deleted workspace-opening tool. For ordinary and still-supported sessions the key was false before, so the IPC/dialog cardinality is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query native window count for a CLOSE shutdown to derive the effective shutdown reason.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one query from each existing lifecycle contribution per CLOSE attempt; unchanged for supported sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary sessions already executed this query because the removed bypass defaulted false; only the retired workspace-opening flow set it true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks shutdown reason evaluation before a possible confirmation dialog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Show the session-shutdown confirmation dialog when an active session would stop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one confirmation per applicable lifecycle veto path and shutdown attempt, unchanged for all remaining flows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dialog was already shown for ordinary active sessions; the only internal bypass setter was deleted with the retired new-workspace tool.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Intentionally blocks shutdown for user confirmation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lifecycle callback per shutdown attempt; active-session checks scale with current session count exactly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The chat and local-agent-host lifecycle vetoes can both participate in a shutdown as before; this PR neither adds callbacks nor increases parallel boundary calls for remaining scenarios.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. The removed context key was transient state, and repository search finds no remaining setter or reader.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: repository search shows the key is gone except as a test literal for another retired name, and the deleted tool contained the sole setter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External code could theoretically set the old raw context-key string, but there is no repository caller and that is not a realistic supported trigger for a performance finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The remaining shutdown path retains the same one-shot IPC and dialog behavior; only an obsolete workflow-specific bypass is removed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 68 changed files, with detailed tracing of activation, dedicated scaffolding, preview materialization, caches, GitHub/model/filesystem boundaries, and shutdown. The PR is a feature retirement composed almost entirely of deletions; it removes eager setup, cache loads, network fan-out, retained preview state, and sequential file work. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or separately evidenced shipped regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
